question: What is the main goal of medical care for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any assistive technology
options.B: To optimize functional independence and well-being
options.C: To confine treatment strictly to acute hospital wards
options.D: To completely cure the underlying congenital condition

explanation: You've got this! We focus on helping patients live their best, most independent lives rather than always chasing a total cure for a permanent condition. Great job!

question: Why can high hospital examination tables be tough for patients with mobility challenges?

options.A: They increase the financial cost of routine blood tests
options.B: They prevent patients with mobility limitations from transferring easily
options.C: They take up too much space in standard nursing stations
options.D: They make it difficult for doctors to hear heart sounds clearly

explanation: Think about a wheelchair user trying to climb up! Fixed high furniture can block access and make simple checks really difficult without proper equipment. You're learning fast!

question: What do we call 'diagnostic overshadowing' when caring for a patient with a disability?

options.A: Overprescribing pain relief medication for chronic joint stiffness
options.B: Failing to document medical history correctly in the patient chart
options.C: Using outdated diagnostic machinery during routine check-ups
options.D: Attributing all new symptoms mistakenly to the existing disability

explanation: It's a sneaky trap! This happens when we assume a new problem is just 'part of their usual condition' and forget to investigate properly. Always look closer!

question: A wheelchair user visits the clinic complaining of unusual fatigue and constant thirst. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Investigate for potential systemic issues like diabetes
options.B: Refer the patient immediately to an orthotic specialist
options.C: Advise the patient to rest more and avoid further medical testing
options.D: Document that fatigue is a normal side effect of using a wheelchair

explanation: Never brush off new symptoms! Fatigue and thirst could mean something like diabetes, so they always deserve a proper check-up. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: Which medical specialty focuses specifically on physical medicine and rehabilitation?
explanation: Physiatrists are the specialists who help patients rebuild their strength and function. Keep this term handy for your exams!

question: Why is nurse coordination so important when a patient is seeing multiple medical specialists?

options.A: To perform advanced surgical procedures in community clinics
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of private specialist consultations
options.C: To replace the need for regular primary healthcare visits
options.D: To prevent conflicting treatment plans and ensure smooth communication

explanation: When too many doctors are involved, advice can clash! As nurses, we bring everything together to keep our patients safe. Brilliant teamwork!

question: Which therapy helps a patient relearn daily skills like cooking, bathing, and dressing?
explanation: Occupational therapists (OTs) are wonderful at helping patients master daily life activities and build personal independence. You nailed it!

question: How can a nurse best support a patient who is going through physical rehabilitation on the ward?

options.A: Limit fluid intake to reduce the need for assisted bathroom trips
options.B: Discourage physical movement until formal therapy sessions resume
options.C: Encourage the patient to perform tasks independently using learned adaptive methods
options.D: Complete all personal care tasks for the patient to save time and prevent fatigue

explanation: We want to empower them! Letting patients practice their skills during routine care builds their confidence and strength. Keep up the great clinical mindset!

question: What is the main difference between an orthosis and a prosthesis?

options.A: An orthosis requires surgery, while a prosthesis is worn externally
options.B: An orthosis is electronic, while a prosthesis is purely mechanical
options.C: An orthosis is used only for children, while prosthetics are for adults
options.D: An orthosis supports an existing limb, while a prosthesis replaces a missing limb

explanation: Easy way to remember: an orthosis (like a brace) supports what's there, while a prosthesis steps in as a replacement limb. You've got this!

question: What common problem can happen if a patient wears a poorly fitted prosthetic limb?
explanation: Friction from ill-fitting gear is tough on fragile skin and can quickly lead to painful sores. Good nursing assessment catches this early!

question: Why do we often use a mix of different therapies to manage chronic pain in patients with physical disabilities?

options.A: Single medications are completely ineffective for all types of nerve pain
options.B: Non-pharmacological methods remove the need for any clinical supervision
options.C: Combining different therapies addresses multiple underlying causes of pain safely
options.D: Pain associated with physical disabilities always resolves spontaneously

explanation: Chronic pain has many layers, so combining meds and physical therapy gives better relief without needing dangerously high drug doses. Smart approach!

question: An adult patient with a severe disability is grimacing and pulling at their clothes during care. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The patient is expressing boredom with the daily routine
options.B: The patient is reacting to normal room temperature changes
options.C: The patient is refusing basic hygiene for personal reasons
options.D: The patient may be experiencing untreated pain or discomfort

explanation: When patients can't easily speak, body language like grimacing or restlessness is our biggest clue that they are hurting. Trust your clinical instincts!

question: What is the main goal of mobile medical outreaches for persons with disabilities in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: To gather statistical research data without providing direct care
options.B: To replace all permanent primary healthcare clinics in the country
options.C: To conduct advanced surgical operations in local village squares
options.D: To bring essential healthcare services and assistive devices closer to underserved populations

explanation: Outreach brings care right to the doorsteps of people who can't easily travel to big city hospitals. Vital work for community health!

question: What is one of the biggest threats to the long-term success of mobile healthcare outreach programs?

options.A: Strict government regulations prohibiting community-level nursing practice
options.B: A complete lack of interest from community members in receiving care
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced diagnostic machinery in rural villages
options.D: Difficulty in sustaining funding and services after initial project phases end

explanation: Many great programs struggle when initial donor funds or temporary support run dry. It's a major challenge in community nursing!

question: What is an important duty for a community health nurse visiting a family with a physically disabled member?

options.A: Providing legal representation in court for disability benefits
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of local community health clinics
options.C: Performing complex orthopedic surgeries within the home environment
options.D: Conducting household assessments and teaching proper transfer techniques

explanation: Home safety checks and teaching family members safe transfer moves keep both the patient and the caregiver safe from injury. Wonderful practice!

question: How does empowering a patient with a physical disability help them through community nursing care?

options.A: It encourages the patient to take an active role in their own healthcare decisions
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future medical or nursing supervision
options.C: It guarantees immediate employment and financial independence
options.D: It removes all environmental barriers found within the public transport system

explanation: Empowerment builds self-advocacy so patients lead the conversation about their own health instead of just sitting back. You're becoming an advocate nurse!
